title: Consultation - Monash College
contextVariants: You are three days from the due date for your Unit 2 research report and you have barely started. You have been unwell for most of the past fortnight but never went to a doctor. You have booked a consultation with Dr Ellery to ask for an extension.

You submitted a draft of your research report last week and got a mark back that was lower than you expected. You do not understand the feedback. You have booked a consultation with Dr Ellery to ask what it means.

The assignment brief for your research report is ambiguous about how broad the topic is allowed to be. You have picked something you are worried is too big. You have booked a consultation with Dr Ellery to check before you commit.
worldFacts: The professor is Dr Ellery. Students may call her Dr Ellery.
The unit is MNET1001 Communication and Research Skills, a first-year unit at Monash College.
The assignment under discussion is the Unit 2 research report.
The report is 2000 words plus or minus ten percent, excluding references. The appendix does not count toward the total.
Referencing style is Harvard.
The report is due 11:55pm on Friday of week 8.
The late penalty is 10 percent of the total mark per day, including weekends.
With documentation, Dr Ellery can grant up to one week. Without documentation the maximum is 72 hours, at her discretion.
Documentation means a medical certificate or a letter from Student Services.
Student Services can register students for ongoing adjustments; they are in Building B, level 2.
Dr Ellery's consultation hours are Tuesday and Thursday, 2pm to 4pm.
There is a tutorial on Thursday morning.
Dr Ellery does not read full drafts during consultation, but will comment on the first two pages if emailed.
The marking rubric rewards analysis over description, and an on-time partial submission scores better than a late complete one.
Group assessment marks can be adjusted individually if a student evidences that a teammate did not contribute.
Before Dr Ellery intervenes in a group dispute, she expects the student to have raised it with the group in writing.
The unit permits AI tools for grammar checking and for testing your own understanding, but not for generating the analysis, and any use must be declared in one sentence at the end of the submission.
Undeclared AI-generated analysis is treated as academic misconduct; declaring it and rewriting it in your own words is not.
Turnitin similarity scores flag quotes and reference lists too, so a high score is not by itself evidence of plagiarism.
The census date for this semester has already passed, so withdrawing now appears on the student's academic record.
Student Services accept walk-ins and can register students for adjustments that apply across all their units.

nodes.speakerLine: Come in, take a seat. Sorry about the mess. So, what did you want to talk about today?
nodes.expectation: The student states their reason for coming: an extension, a question about the brief, or feedback on their work.
nodes.reprompt: Take your time. What brings you in?

branches.label: Asking for an extension
branches.intent: The student wants more time on an assignment, or says they cannot finish by the due date.

branches.label: Confused by the brief
branches.intent: The student does not understand the assignment brief, requirements, scope, or what is being asked of them.

branches.label: Wants feedback on work
branches.intent: The student wants the professor to look at a draft, or to explain a mark or feedback they already received.

branches.label: Group work problem
branches.intent: The student has a problem with their group or a teammate on a group assessment.

branches.label: Academic integrity worry
branches.intent: The student is worried about plagiarism, referencing, or whether their use of AI is allowed.

branches.label: Struggling with the unit
branches.intent: The student is overwhelmed, falling behind generally, or considering withdrawing from the unit.

nodes.speakerLine: An extension. Alright. How long were you after, and what's the reason?
nodes.expectation: The student gives a reason for needing the extension. It may be a solid reason like illness, or a vague one.
nodes.reprompt: How much longer do you need, and why?

branches.label: Concrete reason
branches.intent: The student gives a specific, substantive reason: illness, injury, family emergency, bereavement, mental health, or another genuine hardship.

branches.label: Vague reason
branches.intent: The student is evasive or gives a weak reason: busy, behind, other assignments, forgot, poor planning, work shifts.

branches.label: Asks about the policy first
branches.intent: The student asks how long an extension can be, or what the rules are, before giving a reason.

nodes.speakerLine: Mm. Look, being busy is not by itself grounds for an extension, or I'd be granting them to everyone. Is there something else going on?
nodes.expectation: The student either opens up with a real reason, or accepts the answer and backs down. This is the hard part of the conversation to practise.
nodes.reprompt: I'm asking because if there is a real reason, there are proper channels for it. Is there?

branches.label: Opens up
branches.intent: The student discloses a genuine underlying difficulty they had not mentioned at first.

branches.label: Backs down
branches.intent: The student accepts that they will not get an extension and does not push further.

nodes.speakerLine: Right. I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have any documentation for it? A medical certificate, or something from Student Services?
nodes.expectation: The student says whether they have supporting documentation.
nodes.reprompt: Do you have anything in writing I can attach to the request?

branches.label: Has documentation
branches.intent: The student has, or can obtain, a medical certificate or other supporting document.

branches.label: No documentation
branches.intent: The student has no documentation and did not see a doctor or register with Student Services.

branches.label: Asks what counts
branches.intent: The student asks what documentation is acceptable, or how to get it.

nodes.speakerLine: Good. Send that through to me by Friday and I'll put a week on your due date. Don't leave it any later than Friday, or the request goes to the faculty and out of my hands.
nodes.expectation: Acknowledge and confirm the deadline for sending documentation.
nodes.reprompt: Does that work for you?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student agrees, thanks the professor, or confirms they understand the Friday deadline.

nodes.speakerLine: Without documentation, the most I can give you is seventy-two hours, and that's me using my discretion. I'd also like you to talk to Student Services this week. Can you do that?
nodes.expectation: The student accepts the shorter extension and the condition attached to it, or negotiates.
nodes.reprompt: Seventy-two hours, and a conversation with Student Services. Can you commit to that?

branches.label: Accepts
branches.intent: The student accepts the shorter extension and agrees to contact Student Services.

branches.label: Pushes for more
branches.intent: The student argues that seventy-two hours is not enough and asks for longer.

nodes.speakerLine: I understand, but seventy-two hours is genuinely the limit of what I can do without paperwork. Get the documentation and I can revisit it. That's the honest answer.
nodes.expectation: The student accepts the boundary. Practising hearing no is the point of this branch.
nodes.reprompt: I know it's not what you wanted to hear. Are we alright?

branches.label: Accepts the limit
branches.intent: The student accepts the professor's final position, however reluctantly.

nodes.speakerLine: I appreciate you being straight with me. My advice: submit what you have by the due date. A late-but-complete piece scores worse than an on-time partial one under our rubric.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges the advice.
nodes.reprompt: Does that make sense?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student takes the advice on board.

nodes.speakerLine: Sure. The brief is a bit dense, I'll admit. Which part is giving you trouble?
nodes.expectation: The student identifies a specific part of the brief they are stuck on.
nodes.reprompt: Whereabouts in it are you stuck?

branches.label: Scope of topic
branches.intent: The student is unsure whether their chosen topic is too broad or too narrow.

branches.label: Format or length
branches.intent: The student is asking about word count, structure, referencing style, or formatting.

nodes.speakerLine: Good instinct to ask. Rule of thumb: if you can't state your research question in one sentence without using the word 'and', it's too broad. Narrow it until you can. What's your topic?
nodes.expectation: The student states their topic so the professor can react to it.
nodes.reprompt: What were you planning to write about?

branches.label: States a topic
branches.intent: The student names or describes a topic, however roughly.

nodes.speakerLine: That could work, but I'd cut it in half again. Pick one population, one time period, one outcome. Send me a one-line question by Wednesday and I'll tell you if it's tight enough.
nodes.expectation: The student agrees to send a refined question.
nodes.reprompt: Can you get me one line by Wednesday?

branches.label: Agrees
branches.intent: The student agrees to narrow the topic and send it through.

nodes.speakerLine: Two thousand words, plus or minus ten percent, excluding references. Harvard style. And the appendix doesn't count toward the total, before you ask.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges or asks a follow-up.
nodes.reprompt: Was there anything else on the formatting?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student understands and has no further formatting questions.

nodes.speakerLine: Of course. Is this about the mark you already got back, or do you want me to look at something new?
nodes.expectation: The student clarifies which of the two they mean.
nodes.reprompt: Existing feedback, or something new?

branches.label: Existing mark
branches.intent: The student wants the professor to explain a mark or written feedback they already received.

branches.label: New draft
branches.intent: The student wants the professor to read something they have written but not submitted.

nodes.speakerLine: Let's have a look. My note said your argument was descriptive rather than analytical. Do you know what I meant by that?
nodes.expectation: The student either admits they do not understand, or attempts an explanation. Admitting confusion is the harder social move and the one worth practising.
nodes.reprompt: Be honest with me, did that comment make sense to you?

branches.label: Admits not knowing
branches.intent: The student admits they do not understand the feedback.

branches.label: Attempts an answer
branches.intent: The student offers their own interpretation of the feedback.

nodes.speakerLine: Descriptive tells me what happened. Analytical tells me why it matters and what follows from it. Every paragraph should end with a 'so what'. Try adding that one sentence to each and send it back to me.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges the advice.
nodes.reprompt: Give that a go and see how it reads. Sound alright?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student understands and agrees to revise.

nodes.speakerLine: Happy to. I don't read full drafts during consultation, but if you email it tonight I'll put comments on the first two pages before Thursday. Does that help?
nodes.expectation: The student accepts the offer.
nodes.reprompt: Would that be useful to you?

branches.label: Accepts
branches.intent: The student accepts the offer to email the draft.

nodes.speakerLine: Right. Was there anything else while you're here?
nodes.expectation: The student closes the conversation politely, or raises one more thing.
nodes.reprompt: Anything else, or are we done?

branches.label: Nothing else
branches.intent: The student says they have nothing further and thanks the professor.

branches.label: One more thing
branches.intent: The student raises an additional question or topic.

branches.label: Thanks the professor warmly
branches.intent: The student expresses genuine relief or gratitude beyond a simple no.

nodes.speakerLine: Go on then, quickly. I've got another student at half past.
nodes.expectation: The student asks their additional question concisely.
nodes.reprompt: What was it?

branches.label: Asks it
branches.intent: The student asks any further question.

nodes.speakerLine: Alright. Good on you for coming in and asking rather than guessing. That's the whole point of these. I'll see you in the tutorial on Thursday.
nodes.expectation: End of conversation.

nodes.speakerLine: Fair question. With documentation I can give you up to a week. Without it, seventy-two hours is my limit. Anything longer goes to the faculty. So - which are we talking about?
nodes.expectation: The student now gives their reason, knowing the policy.
nodes.reprompt: So what's the reason you need it?

branches.label: Concrete reason
branches.intent: The student gives a genuine reason: illness, injury, family emergency, bereavement, mental health.

branches.label: Vague reason
branches.intent: The student gives a weak or evasive reason: busy, behind, poor planning, work.

nodes.speakerLine: A medical certificate from any GP is fine, or a letter from Student Services if you're registered with them. A screenshot of a booking isn't enough on its own - it needs to say you were unfit to study.
nodes.expectation: The student says whether they can get that.
nodes.reprompt: So - can you get me something like that?

branches.label: Can get it
branches.intent: The student says they have documentation or can obtain it.

branches.label: Cannot get it
branches.intent: The student cannot obtain documentation.

nodes.speakerLine: Group work. Right, that's half the emails I get. What's actually happening?
nodes.expectation: The student describes the group problem: a teammate not contributing, a disagreement, or scheduling.
nodes.reprompt: What's going on with the group?

branches.label: Teammate not contributing
branches.intent: One or more group members are not doing their share of the work.

branches.label: Disagreement in the group
branches.intent: The group disagrees about direction, approach, or quality of work.

branches.label: Cannot organise meetings
branches.intent: The group cannot find time to meet or coordinate.

nodes.speakerLine: That's frustrating, and it's more common than people admit. Have you raised it with them directly yet?
nodes.expectation: The student says whether they have already spoken to the teammate.
nodes.reprompt: Have you actually said something to them about it?

branches.label: Has raised it
branches.intent: The student has already spoken to the teammate and it did not resolve.

branches.label: Has not raised it
branches.intent: The student has not spoken to the teammate yet, often out of awkwardness.

nodes.speakerLine: Then that's your first step, and I know it's the uncomfortable one. Message the group, be specific about what's outstanding, and put a date on it. Keep it in writing so there's a record.
nodes.expectation: The student agrees to speak to the group first.
nodes.reprompt: Can you have that conversation this week?

branches.label: Agrees
branches.intent: The student accepts the advice to raise it with the group directly.

branches.label: Reluctant
branches.intent: The student resists, doubts it will work, or is anxious about confrontation.

nodes.speakerLine: I understand. But if it does come to me reallocating marks, the first thing I'll ask for is evidence you tried to sort it out. A polite message in the group chat is that evidence. It protects you.
nodes.expectation: The student accepts that raising it is worth doing.
nodes.reprompt: Does that make sense as a reason to do it?

branches.label: Accepts
branches.intent: The student accepts the reasoning and will raise it.

nodes.speakerLine: Good - then you've done your part. Forward me the messages and I'll contact them directly. If it doesn't change, I can mark contributions individually. Nobody carries a group on their own in my unit.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges, or asks what happens next.
nodes.reprompt: Send me those messages and I'll take it from there. Alright?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student is satisfied and will send the evidence.

nodes.speakerLine: Disagreement isn't automatically a problem - it usually means people care. What I'd do is write down the two options, list what each costs you in time, and decide as a group against the rubric rather than against each other.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges or pushes back.
nodes.reprompt: Try that and see whether it settles it. Sound workable?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student accepts the suggestion.

nodes.speakerLine: You don't all need to be in a room. Split the work into pieces that can be done alone, agree the interfaces in writing, and meet once a week for twenty minutes. Most groups over-meet and under-decide.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges.
nodes.reprompt: Would that work for your group?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student accepts the suggestion.

nodes.speakerLine: And if it's still unresolved a week out from the due date, come back to me. Don't leave it until the night before - that's when my options run out.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges.
nodes.reprompt: Come back to me if it doesn't improve. Alright?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student agrees to come back if needed.

nodes.speakerLine: I'd rather you ask than guess, so - what's the concern?
nodes.expectation: The student says whether it is about AI use or about referencing and plagiarism.
nodes.reprompt: What is it you're worried about?

branches.label: Used AI
branches.intent: The student used or wants to use an AI tool and is unsure whether that is permitted.

branches.label: Referencing or plagiarism
branches.intent: The student is worried about citing sources, similarity scores, or accidental plagiarism.

nodes.speakerLine: Alright. The unit's position is that you may use it to check grammar or to test your own understanding, but the analysis has to be yours, and you declare any use. So tell me honestly - what did you use it for?
nodes.expectation: The student admits what they used AI for. Honesty here is the skill being practised.
nodes.reprompt: What did you actually use it for?

branches.label: Editing or understanding
branches.intent: The student used AI for grammar, proofreading, explaining a concept, or checking their own understanding.

branches.label: Generating content
branches.intent: The student used AI to write part of the actual argument or content.

nodes.speakerLine: That's within the rules. Add a line at the end saying what you used and what for - one sentence is enough. Declaring it is what keeps it above board.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges.
nodes.reprompt: Add that declaration and you're fine. Clear?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student understands and will declare it.

nodes.speakerLine: Right - I'm glad you told me. That part has to be rewritten in your own words, because as it stands it isn't your analysis and the rubric marks your analysis. Do that before you submit and there's no misconduct issue. Hide it and there is.
nodes.expectation: The student accepts and agrees to rewrite.
nodes.reprompt: Rewrite that section and declare the rest. Can you do that?

branches.label: Accepts
branches.intent: The student accepts and will rewrite the section.

nodes.speakerLine: Similarity scores frighten people more than they should - quotes and reference lists both flag. What matters is whether an idea that isn't yours is attributed. Where are you unsure?
nodes.expectation: The student describes what they are unsure about.
nodes.reprompt: Which bit are you unsure about?

branches.label: Describes the worry
branches.intent: The student explains their referencing concern, however roughly.

nodes.speakerLine: Then cite it. The rule I give everyone: if you knew it before you started reading, it's yours. If you learned it from something, it gets a citation. Over-citing has never cost anyone a mark in my unit.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges.
nodes.reprompt: Cite it and you're safe. Alright?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student understands.

nodes.speakerLine: Okay. Thank you for telling me - that's not an easy thing to say out loud. How long have you been feeling like this?
nodes.expectation: The student says how long they have been struggling.
nodes.reprompt: How long has it been like this?

branches.label: Recently
branches.intent: The student says it is recent, a few weeks, or since a specific event.

branches.label: All semester
branches.intent: The student says it has been ongoing since the start, or a long time.

nodes.speakerLine: That's a long time to carry on your own. I'm going to be straight with you: this is bigger than one assignment, and it's not something you and I can fix in a twenty-minute consultation.
nodes.expectation: The student responds to being told they need more support.
nodes.reprompt: Does that sound fair?

branches.label: Accepts
branches.intent: The student accepts that they need more support.

branches.label: Deflects
branches.intent: The student downplays it or insists they are fine.

nodes.speakerLine: Maybe. But you came in here and said it, and people don't usually say that when nothing's wrong. I'm not going to push - I'd just rather you talked to someone who does this properly than to me.
nodes.expectation: The student accepts a referral.
nodes.reprompt: Would you be willing to talk to someone?

branches.label: Accepts
branches.intent: The student agrees to seek support.

nodes.speakerLine: Student Services are in Building B, level two, and you can walk in - you don't need an appointment. They can also register you for adjustments that apply across all your units, not just mine. Will you go this week?
nodes.expectation: The student commits to contacting support, or asks about the unit itself.
nodes.reprompt: Will you go and see them this week?

branches.label: Will go
branches.intent: The student agrees to contact Student Services.

branches.label: Asks about dropping
branches.intent: The student asks about withdrawing from the unit or the consequences of doing so.

nodes.speakerLine: You can withdraw without academic penalty up to the census date, which has passed for this semester - so a withdrawal now shows on your record. That's not the end of the world, but it's a decision to make with an adviser, not in a corridor.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges.
nodes.reprompt: Talk to an adviser before you decide anything. Alright?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student accepts the advice to talk to an adviser first.

nodes.speakerLine: And as for this unit - submit what you have by Friday, even if it's incomplete. A partial submission on time scores better than nothing, and it keeps your options open while you sort the rest out.
nodes.expectation: The student acknowledges.
nodes.reprompt: Get me something by Friday, even if it's rough. Can you do that?

branches.label: Acknowledges
branches.intent: The student agrees to submit what they have.

nodes.speakerLine: You're welcome. And for what it's worth - the students who come and ask are the ones who tend to be fine. It's the ones who don't that worry me.
nodes.expectation: The student closes the conversation.
nodes.reprompt: Anything else before you go?

branches.label: Closes
branches.intent: The student says goodbye or has nothing further.
